# The five-beat tour rejects its committed popup target

## Context
The DockLayouts NL census in #17844 reports the five-beat journey stopping before its popup proxy appears. An unchanged headed run at `5dc6b80feffed2e1da1e91bc31a3ccb0d8a17094` independently reproduces the same failure in scenes 3, 4 and 5. The full file selected 11 tests: 5 passed, 5 failed, 1 skipped.

## The Problem
The proxy timeout hides an earlier refusal. Through the live Neural Link, `executeTearOutStep({itemId:'metrics',sourceNodeId:'right-top-tabs'})` succeeds with `transferCommitted:true`. Calling `executeCrossWindowDockStep` for Commits into that vessel immediately returns `target vessel is not an available first-dock workspace`.

The Metrics PopupWorkspace has `runtimeState.committed:true` and its own live `participation`; `runtimeState.participation` is absent. The tour still rejects committed targets and later reads participation from runtime state.

## The Architectural Reality
- `apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs:onTearOutDocumentChange` transfers the first pane through the Group and then sets `state.committed = true`.
- `apps/workstation/view/PopupWorkspace.mjs:syncParticipation` owns the popup interaction participant.
- `apps/workstation/tour/NativeGestureDriver.mjs:executeCrossWindowDockStep` retains the earlier first-dock admission and participation reads.
- `CrossWindowGestureSnapshot.mjs:readCrossWindowGestureSnapshot` already resolves the participant through `state.host`.

## The Fix
Bring the existing native gesture driver onto the committed popup owner. Keep real input, the single-claim/preview/proxy evidence, semantic transfer and stack-return checks. Add targeted regression controls to the existing GestureDriver unit spec. Make the journey expose an executor refusal instead of masking it behind a proxy timeout. The repaired conversion then exposed an obsolete completion read: the popup's engine-default transfer adopts both documents and retires the source, but does not call the root's optional transfer hook. Observe the fresh Group history row and await the involved Workspace projections after release; preserve root native-close metadata only for that exact transaction. Match the current return-phase vocabulary while retaining the physical topology-exit/window-gone checks. No runtime commit routing change, lifecycle abstraction, or compatibility alias.

## Contract Ledger
| Surface | Authority | Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| NativeGestureDriver cross-window step | Workspace tear-out commit and PopupWorkspace participation | A connected, committed target can receive the second gesture; readiness reads the live host | Missing/uncommitted/closing targets refuse before input | Existing method JSDoc | Positive committed target plus refused controls; whole-file headed journey |

| Tour transfer receipt | Transaction Group history and Workspace refresh promises | Read a fresh matching transfer without depending on a root callback; retain matching native-close metadata | Stale or unrelated rows yield no receipt; no history means no history-backed witness | NativeGestureDriver method JSDoc | Real popup transfer with absent root receipt; stale and wrong-target controls |

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A committed first vessel is admitted by the cross-window tour driver; an uncommitted, missing, or closing target is refused before input.
- [ ] Gesture readiness uses the popup host's current participation, without adding a runtime-state alias.
- [ ] Unit controls fail on the original driver and pass on the repair.
- [ ] The full five-beat file runs headed with the Brain runtime; scenes 3–5 retain their proxy, transfer, identity and return assertions. Any newly exposed independent defect is recorded with its actual receipt.
- [ ] An early driver refusal is reported by the staging helper without an unobserved popup-wait rejection.
- [ ] The tour observes a fresh matching Group transaction when the popup uses the engine default commit path; stale or unrelated rows cannot satisfy it. Native-close metadata is retained only for that transaction.

## Out of Scope
The separate showcase source-node mismatch and source-continuity render failure in the baseline; film production and portability claims; engine Group/native close refactoring.

## Avoided Traps
Do not delete the proxy assertion: the Workstation still supplies that drag embodiment. Do not make a committed popup look uncommitted or copy participation back onto runtime state.

## Decision Record impact
Aligned-with ADR 0029; no semantic ownership or wire change.
